title: Lattice Yang–Mills foundations: gauge invariance and classical vacua of the Wilson action for unitary representations
claim: On the periodic hypercubic lattice (ℤ/Lℤ)^d, for an arbitrary group G with link variables U : site → direction → G and gauge action U_{x,μ} ↦ g_x U_{x,μ} g_{x+μ}⁻¹, the Lean theorem Contribution.result proves: (1) the plaquette holonomy transforms by conjugation at its base point, so every plaquette action ∑_x ∑_{μ<ν} f(U_p) with a class function f is exactly gauge invariant; (2) for any unitary representation ρ : G → M_n(ℂ) (unitary-valued and multiplicative, predicate IsUnitaryRep), the Wilson action S_ρ(U) = ∑_x ∑_{μ<ν} (n − Re tr ρ(U_p)) is gauge invariant and nonnegative, and S_ρ(U) = 0 iff ρ(U_p) = 1 for every plaquette (all orientations); if ρ is injective, S_ρ(U) = 0 iff U is flat (every plaquette holonomy is 1); (3) for unitary V, 2(n − Re tr V) = ∑_{i,j} |(V − 1)_{ij}|², i.e. the Wilson weight is half the squared Frobenius distance to the identity. Why it matters: these are the exact classical inputs to the lattice route to the mass gap (Wilson 1974; Osterwalder–Seiler strong coupling; Chatterjee's probabilistic program). The identity in (3) gives the coercivity ‖V−1‖² ≤ 2·cost used in small-field / weak-coupling analysis, and (2) identifies the minimizers of the Wilson action — the classical vacua around which any weak-coupling or continuum-limit argument must expand — for every compact gauge group presented through a faithful unitary representation (SU(n), SO(n), Sp(n), and by Peter–Weyl every compact Lie group). The theorem is a reusable, dependency-free bundle in the track's pinned Lean 4.36 / Mathlib environment.
novelty: This is the first contribution on this track, so no accepted track results overlap. The mathematics is classical: gauge invariance of the Wilson action is due to Wilson (1974) and is textbook material. Outside this track, Michael R. Douglas's Lean library lgt (github.com/mrdouglasny/lgt, Lean 4.30) already formalizes U(n) Wilson lattice gauge theory, gauge invariance of its Wilson action, the bound Re tr U ≤ n, and a strong-coupling mass-gap theorem. Searching lgt at commit b8793ccf for vacuum or flatness statements, Frobenius identities and faithful-representation hypotheses found none of the following, which are this bundle's increments: the exact identity n − Re tr V = ½‖V − 1‖²_F; the characterization of the zero set of the Wilson action (plaquettes in ker ρ; flat configurations for faithful ρ, including both plaquette orientations via U_p(ν,μ) = U_p(μ,ν)⁻¹); and the statement for an abstract gauge group through a unitary representation rather than U(n) alone. The formal code is original and independent of lgt; no lgt source was copied.

limitations: This is classical, finite-lattice infrastructure. It proves nothing about the quantum theory: no Haar/Gibbs measure, no reflection positivity, transfer matrix, correlation decay or mass gap, and no continuum limit, so it does not address the existence or mass-gap parts of the Clay problem. The zero-set result identifies flat configurations, not gauge orbits: on the torus a flat configuration need not be gauge-equivalent to the trivial one (nontrivial holonomy around noncontractible cycles), and the statement 'flat implies pure gauge' on simply connected regions is not proved. Compact simple groups enter only through a supplied unitary representation ρ : G → M_n(ℂ); the existence of a faithful unitary representation (Peter–Weyl) and any topology or Lie structure on G are not formalized. The lattice is periodic and hypercubic; the action uses the fundamental-representation Wilson weight only, with no coupling constant normalization.
